name: North Macedonia

findings.summary: Huawei and ZTE supplied equipment for the existing 3G and 4G networks of both North Macedonian mobile operators; contract dates were undisclosed and one operator was expected to keep Chinese 3G/4G gear into part of 2023.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 5 as operational installed base. Single opened S3 source (an NGO fact-checking outlet), so uncorroborated and low confidence. Which operator uses which vendor, and in which segments (RAN, core, transport), is not stated. Date is the reporting date, not deployment date; retirement status after 2023 not established.

findings.summary: Ericsson won the 5G infrastructure procurements of both Makedonski Telekom and A1 Makedonija and was installing base stations, with Makedonski Telekom expecting its Ericsson-led modernisation to finish in early 2023.
findings.analyst_inference: Ericsson (Sweden) is an EU vendor, so pole third. Single opened S3 source; no operator or Ericsson release opened, so uncorroborated and low. Contract values and award dates not found. Whether the modernisation removed Huawei/ZTE from 4G (a de facto swap) is implied by the source's framing but not confirmed, so no reversal coded.

findings.controller: United States Government (Department of State, Clean Network)
findings.local_actor: Government of North Macedonia (PM Zoran Zaev)
findings.summary: North Macedonia and the United States signed a memorandum of understanding on 5G security stressing trusted suppliers, reported as joining the US Clean Network initiative; the electronic communications law was amended in April 2021 to add network-security powers.

sources.publisher: CHOICE (China Observers in Central and Eastern Europe)

findings.analyst_inference: Tier 1: non-binding MOU. Pole us as alignment with the US trusted-vendor framework; it is not an equipment deployment. Opened sources are S3 and S4 (think tank), no S1/S2, so not corroborated. The April 2021 amendment and autumn 2021 regulator supplier-risk rules are not shown to name or exclude any vendor, so no ban is coded.

findings.local_actor: One Macedonia Telecommunications DOOEL (4iG Group, Hungary)
findings.summary: One Macedonia, a 4iG Group subsidiary and the country's newest mobile operator, signed supply and service contracts with Ericsson for a greenfield 5G Standalone network, RAN and core, over 500 base stations across 2026-2029.
findings.analyst_inference: Equipment vendor Ericsson sets pole third; operator owner 4iG is Hungarian. Világgazdaság and IntelliNews appear to restate the 4iG release, so not treated as independent corroboration; single opened S1 permits medium. EUR 100m is 4iG's country investment strategy, not the contract price, so values null. Follows a Sept 2025 LOI; spectrum licence awarded 23 Jan 2026.

findings.controller: EuroHPC JU / European AI Factories network (host supercomputers outside North Macedonia)
findings.local_actor: Faculty of Computer Science and Engineering (FINKI), Ss. Cyril and Methodius University; Ministry of Digital Transformation
findings.financier: EU (Horizon Europe / EuroHPC, ~EUR 3.1m) and Government of North Macedonia (co-financing)
findings.summary: North Macedonia launched Vezilka, a EUR 6.2m national AI centre led by FINKI with the digital ministry, half EU-funded, affiliated to Greece's Pharos AI Factory to give local users access to European supercomputers over three years.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 2: a funded project launch with no local compute specified. Pole third because the compute is accessed from EU-hosted supercomputers (Pharos, Greece), not owned locally; reviewer may prefer domestic for the centre itself. BTA is a state news agency, so S4; not corroborated. Values in EUR not converted. Hardware vendor unknown.

silicon.null_reason: no dedicated search; no accelerator purchases surfaced in facilities/AI-centre searches (Vezilka names no hardware)

models.null_reason: two searches found no frontier-provider partnership or national model; a 2023 government AI assistant ('Ada') names no underlying model or vendor, and Macedonian-language model plans name no partner

applications.null_reason: one search on safe-city/surveillance found no documented Huawei/Hikvision/Dahua system in North Macedonia; regional reporting opened covers Serbia, not North Macedonia

research_gaps: Which vendor (Huawei or ZTE) serves which operator's 4G RAN and core, and has Chinese equipment been fully removed from Makedonski Telekom and A1 Makedonija since 2023?
CHOICE (Jan 2021) relays local reports that Huawei was top-ranked in a Makedonski Telekom 5G tender that was put on hold; was that tender cancelled for security reasons (a possible reversal)?
Do the April 2021 electronic-communications amendments or AEK's 2021 supplier risk-profile rules designate any high-risk vendor?
Who are the 5-6 data-centre investors the PM cited (Aug 2026), and the status and contractor of the reported EUR 20m state data centre targeted for 2027?
What model or vendor underlies the government's 'Ada' digital assistant (2023)?
Any Chinese-supplied safe-city or police CCTV in Skopje or other municipalities (not found in one search).
